```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```

```{r data-import, include=FALSE}
# Delete this chunk after merging with A's Rmd.
clean <- read.csv(
  file.path("data", "hotels_clean.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r variable-coding, include=FALSE}
model_data <- clean
model_data$hotel <- relevel(factor(model_data$hotel), ref = "City Hotel")
model_data$arrival_date_month <- factor(
  model_data$arrival_date_month,
  levels = month.name
)
model_data$meal <- relevel(factor(model_data$meal), ref = "BB")
model_data$market_segment <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$market_segment),
  ref = "Online TA"
)
model_data$customer_type <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$customer_type),
  ref = "Transient"
)
model_data$reserved_room_type <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$reserved_room_type),
  ref = "A"
)
model_data$is_repeated_guest <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$is_repeated_guest),
  ref = "No"
)
model_data$domestic <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$domestic),
  ref = "International"
)
```

# Preliminary model

```{r model, include=FALSE}
model <- lm(
  adr ~ lead_time * hotel +
    arrival_date_month +
    stays_in_weekend_nights +
    stays_in_week_nights +
    adults +
    children +
    meal +
    market_segment +
    customer_type +
    reserved_room_type +
    is_repeated_guest +
    total_of_special_requests +
    domestic,
  data = model_data
)

model_summary <- summary(model)
```

The preliminary multiple linear regression model included 14 predictors and a lead-time-by-hotel interaction.

```{r model-table}
coefficient_matrix <- coef(model_summary)
confidence_intervals <- confint(model)

coefficient_table <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(coefficient_matrix),
  Estimate = coefficient_matrix[, "Estimate"],
  SE = coefficient_matrix[, "Std. Error"],
  Lower_95_CI = confidence_intervals[, 1],
  Upper_95_CI = confidence_intervals[, 2],
  p_value = coefficient_matrix[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
  row.names = NULL
)

coefficient_table[, 2:5] <- round(coefficient_table[, 2:5], 3)
coefficient_table$p_value <- format.pval(
  coefficient_table$p_value,
  digits = 3,
  eps = 0.001
)

knitr::kable(
  coefficient_table,
  caption = "Preliminary multiple linear regression estimates for ADR, with standard errors and 95% confidence intervals."
)
```

```{r main-results, include=FALSE}
model_estimates <- coef(model)
interaction_term <- "lead_time:hotelResort Hotel"

city_slope <- unname(model_estimates["lead_time"])
interaction_estimate <- unname(model_estimates[interaction_term])
resort_slope <- city_slope + interaction_estimate

city_ci <- confidence_intervals["lead_time", ]
interaction_ci <- confidence_intervals[interaction_term, ]
```

At the City Hotel, one additional day of lead time was associated with a `r abs(round(city_slope, 4))`-euro lower mean ADR (95% CI: `r round(city_ci[1], 4)`, `r round(city_ci[2], 4)`), holding the other predictors fixed. The interaction estimate was `r round(interaction_estimate, 4)` euros (95% CI: `r round(interaction_ci[1], 4)`, `r round(interaction_ci[2], 4)`), giving a Resort Hotel slope of `r round(resort_slope, 4)` euros per day. Longer lead times were associated with lower ADR at both hotels, but the negative association was weaker at the Resort Hotel. The significant interaction was consistent with Abrate et al. (2012), who found that inter-temporal hotel pricing varies with hotel and customer characteristics. The adjusted R-squared was `r round(model_summary$adj.r.squared, 4)`. These estimates describe associations, not causal effects.

# Residual analysis

```{r residual-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Residual plots for the preliminary model: (a) residuals versus fitted ADR, (b) residuals versus lead time, and (c) the normal Q-Q plot."}
model_residuals <- residuals(model)
fitted_values <- fitted(model)

old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

plot(
  fitted_values,
  model_residuals,
  xlab = "Fitted ADR",
  ylab = "Residual",
  main = "(a) Residuals vs fitted",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

plot(
  model_data$lead_time,
  model_residuals,
  xlab = "Lead time (days)",
  ylab = "Residual",
  main = "(b) Residuals vs lead time",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

qqnorm(
  model_residuals,
  main = "(c) Normal Q-Q",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15)
)
qqline(model_residuals, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

In our preliminary model,systematic structure and increasing spread can be seen in the residuals-fitted and residuals-lead-time plots, shows the linearity and constant variance assumptions are questionable. The available data do not contain enough identifying information to verify the uncorrelated-errors assumption. The Q-Q plot is heavy tailed, gives the evidence that the normality assumption may not be reasonable.
